summary.text: Adam Gray is the Democratic incumbent for California's 13th Congressional District, a Central Valley seat. Born and raised in Merced, he worked as a legislative aide and university lecturer, served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022, and lost a 2022 House race before winning the seat in 2024 by 187 votes. His official biography says he is on the House Agriculture and Natural Resources Committees and is Whip of the Blue Dog Coalition.

paragraphs.text: Gray was born in Merced, California, in 1977; his official biography says he was born and raised there and still lives in the city.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of California at Santa Barbara.

Before his election to the Assembly he worked as a legislative aide in the California State Legislature and as an assistant lecturer at the University of California at Merced; his official biography describes him as an educator at UC Merced.
Gray represented Merced and Stanislaus Counties in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022.

According to his official biography, he founded the California Problem Solvers Caucus in Sacramento and worked on establishing a medical school program at UC Merced, new water storage infrastructure and improved water access for Central Valley farmers.
In November 2022 Gray lost the general election for California's 13th Congressional District to John Duarte, 50.2% to 49.8% (67,060 to 66,496 votes).
He defeated Duarte, then the incumbent, in the November 2024 rematch, 105,554 votes to 105,367, and took office on January 3, 2025.
In Congress he serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Natural Resources and is Whip of the Blue Dog Coalition, according to his official biography.
